issue_context.title: Tuya Thermostat for Airton HVAC doesn't switch to "heat" mode
issue_context.body:
### The problem

With a HVAC of the brand Airton which embed a Wifi module, it is not possible to set the mode to "heat".
When doing this, the mode is set to "heat_cool" which is not what is expected.

With the remote command, when I set to "heat" mode, the Tuya climate integration is succesfully set to "heat".

So the bug is only when sending the "heat" mode to the HVAC and not when displaying the mode.

I notice also that when sending the:
- "auto" mode, the HVAC is set to "heat",
- "dry" mode, the HVAC is set to "cool",
- "fan only" mode, the HVAC is set to "cool",

There seems to be a mismatch in the mapping of the mode.

See entity named climate.clim_chambre_parents_tuya

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2022.9.5

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Tuya

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/tuya

### Diagnostics information

[config_entry-tuya-0c08ee0cf91155f513a6d3af7e72dd5a.json (1).txt](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/9604940/config_entry-tuya-0c08ee0cf91155f513a6d3af7e72dd5a.json.1.txt)

Hey there @tuya, @zlinoliver, @frenck, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`tuya`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L1169) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

I could find that the "Dry" button sometimes put the HVAC into heat mode. But it is not every time curiously.
This shows the "mapping problem" explained above.

there are more issues as this one:
#81681, #72852, #60646, #62839, #59529

Hello, I was trying to debug by adding logs in debug mode and it seems it is cloud relative issue.
The command sends by the integration seems good.
Example while switching to heat mode:

```
2023-01-31 15:33:14.041 WARNING (SyncWorker_0) [homeassistant.components.tuya.climate] commands that will be send are: [{'code': <DPCode.SWITCH: 'switch'>, 'value': True}, {'code': <DPCode.MODE: 'mode'>, 'value': 'heat'}]
2023-01-31 15:33:14.042 WARNING (SyncWorker_0) [tuya_iot.device] Sending commands [{'code': <DPCode.SWITCH: 'switch'>, 'value': True}, {'code': <DPCode.MODE: 'mode'>, 'value': 'heat'}] to device xxxxxxxx
```

I see here: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/82056 that this should be fixed now. But this is not the case for me.
It is better but switching to heat doesn't do anything typically

When I check on the IOT Tuya platform I can confirm that the heat command is not valid:
When sending heat:
![Capture d’écran 2023-01-31 à 17 14 26](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1712374/215817301-9e6c870b-c1c2-485d-a306-9489bac6b875.png)


When sending 'cold':
![Capture d’écran 2023-01-31 à 17 13 34](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1712374/215816979-1d57d4de-86aa-4a7d-80ed-15012f235a29.png)

I try to find the correct value to be able to fix

The documentation says heat should be a valid command:
```

{
        "code": "mode",
        "desc": "{\"range\":[\"auto\",\"cold\",\"wet\",\"heat\",\"fan\"]}",
        "name": "工作模式",
        "type": "Enum",
        "values": "{\"range\":[\"auto\",\"cold\",\"wet\",\"heat\",\"fan\"]}"
      },
```

The allowed mode seems to be 'hot' and not 'heat' in my case.

```
    {
      "code": "mode",
      "value": "hot"
    },
```

When I look at the declaration of the mode in the case I see this:

```
TUYA_HVAC_TO_HA = {
    "auto": HVACMode.HEAT_COOL,
    "cold": HVACMode.COOL,
    "freeze": HVACMode.COOL,
    "heat": HVACMode.HEAT,
    "hot": HVACMode.HEAT,
    "manual": HVACMode.HEAT_COOL,
    "wet": HVACMode.DRY,
    "wind": HVACMode.FAN_ONLY,
}
```

So 'hot' is never send to the device. It is always 'heat' which is not a recognise command for this device
I try to hard code 'hot' for the command but it is not accepted too :(

After contacting the Tuya support, I have to change the control instruction mode in the Tuya interface directly and all is coming back to normal working.

This can be done like this:
![Capture d’écran 2023-02-03 à 08 57 25](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1712374/216543944-7f4a0cfd-4bc4-4624-b654-98282c041b4b.png)

![Capture d’écran 2023-02-03 à 08 57 42](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1712374/216544000-5f9e7697-5b59-4225-b905-e1dc49da9f63.png)

![Capture d’écran 2023-02-03 à 08 57 59](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1712374/216544053-51d8ea8d-55cb-40cb-b011-449dc99a9746.png)

Save and wait 24h, and on my case, it works. I don't really understand why and what I have done but it works. Maybe this can help others.

Finally switching to DP instruction set fix the heat command but breaks the switch command (to set hvac_mode on or off).

Will be fixed by a futur PR.

review_comments:
This seems to be device/manufacturer specific, as this is not a normal DP name.  (capitalized).

Please note, that we don't want to add/implement device specifics, but only use Tuya standardized data points. Have you contacted Tuya about this?

Yes TuYa, have been contacted. You have the result here: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/78815#issuecomment-1415277555
The contact of TuYa is the origin of this PR. Devices have 2 modes: standard instruction set or original DP instruction. This PR is made to make the "original TP instruction set" works.
@frenck  is this a blocker point ? If yes I will not try to fix your suggestion below and stop this PR.

A second opinion is needed here. Are these two opinions exclusive? What should we do if a device supports both?

@jmcollin78 Does your device include `DPCode.SWITCH` in `self.device.function`?

Maybe we could extend the if statement to 
```suggestion
        if DPCode.POWER_SWITCH in self.device.function and not DPCode.SWITCH in self.device.function:
```

Before applying this suggestion, wait for another opinion.
No. My device have only DPCode.POWER in function.

The device can be configured in standard instruction set (the previous "mode") or original DP instruction set which include the "POWER". The device cannot have both.
See more explaination here if needed : https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/78815

This PR fixes this issue.
Thus, your last proposal will not change anything.

Device are only in one mode possible : POWER or SWITCH. We can change this putting the device into Native CP mode on the TuYA cloud. This is explain here: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/78815

So for me, your last proposal is useless.
This ain't right, we have helper methods for this, please use the find_dpcode methods to find them.
